sources.summary: The only supplied input. No IT procedure, SLA, category list, team names or tenant read were available; country, language and access model are assumptions recorded as decisions.

sections.title: Self-service IT request form
sections.summary: Any employee submits an IT request themselves; submission creates a case.

sections.title: Clear confirmation
sections.summary: The requester must be told what was recorded and what happens next.

groups.name: IT Support
groups.purpose: Proposed team that triages and resolves self-service IT requests. Real name and members not supplied (decision D2).

flags.detail: No source names the IT team or its members; placeholder pending D2.

workflows.name: IT request

grants.reason: Self-service: any employee opens their own IT request. Assumption from the request wording; no source lists exceptions (decision D1).

access.note: IT Support receives no view grant by default: assignees see the cases that carry their actions. Whether the team needs every case as a shared queue is decision D2.

actions.name: Triage the IT request
actions.description:
Task: Classify the request and set its priority so the right technician can pick it up.
How: 1. Read `request_type`, `summary`, `details` and `urgency` submitted by the requester, and open the attachment if there is one. 2. Correct `request_type` if the requester chose the wrong option. 3. Set `priority` from the impact described, not only from the requester's `urgency`. 4. If something essential is missing, ask the requester in a case comment and wait for the answer before completing.
Evidence: `priority` filled and a comment stating the classification and, when changed, why `request_type` was corrected.
Done when: `priority` is set and the request is clear enough to be resolved without further questions.
Exceptions: If the request is not an IT matter, comment which team handles it and cancel the case; do not resolve work that belongs to another area.

actions.name: Resolve the IT request
actions.description:
Task: Do the work the request asks for and record what was done.
How: 1. Read the triage comment and `priority`. 2. Perform the change, installation, repair or access grant. 3. Write a resolution comment the requester can understand: what was done and anything they must do on their side.
Evidence: The resolution comment on the case; for access requests, the approval document attached by the requester or by you.
Done when: The requester can do what they asked for and the resolution comment is on the case.
Exceptions: If the work needs approval, equipment or a supplier that is not available, comment the blocker and the expected path; do not complete the action until the work is actually done.

actions.name: Confirm the resolution
actions.description:
Task: Confirm whether the IT request was solved.
How: 1. Open the case and read the resolution comment left by IT Support. 2. Check that you can now do what you asked for. 3. Answer the "Resolution confirmation" form.
Evidence: The submitted "Resolution confirmation" response with `resolution_accepted` filled.
Done when: The response is submitted.
Exceptions: If the request is not solved, answer "No" and describe what still fails in `resolution_feedback`; IT Support reopens the work from your answer.

setupNotes: Placeholder workflow created by provia-form-designer so the intake form has a destination; the action set, decisions and routing still need provia-workflow-designer. No YAML was produced.

Case metadata the intake form maps to (declare in the workflow): request_type (select), summary (text), details (rich_text), urgency (select), affected_asset (text), department (text), needed_by (date), attachment (file), contact_phone (phone); set by IT: priority (select); set by the closing form: resolution_accepted (boolean), resolution_feedback (text).
Form intake and Form Fill links are configured in Provia after the workflow draft exists; verify each field mapping there (see it-request-form.md §4 and §7).
File size limit for `attachment`: verify the destination limit before writing a number into the form help text.
Confirmation text is in it-request-form.md §6; where it is displayed (confirmation screen, notification) depends on the destination form configuration (decision D5).

forms.title: Self-service IT request

fields.label: What do you need?
fields.helpText: Choose the closest option. IT will reclassify it if needed.

options.label: Access to a system or folder

fields.label: Short title
fields.helpText: One line IT can read in a list, e.g. "VPN fails on Windows laptop".

fields.label: Describe the request
fields.helpText: What you are trying to do, what happens instead, and any error message. For access requests, name the system and the access level.

fields.label: How urgent is this?
fields.helpText: This is your view of the impact. IT sets the final priority during triage.

options.label: I can wait a few days
I cannot work until it is solved

fields.label: Asset tag or device
fields.helpText: The sticker on the device, if it has one.

fields.label: Your department
fields.note: Free text until a department list is supplied (decision D3).

fields.label: Needed by
fields.helpText: Only if there is a real date (a start date, a trip, a deadline). Leaving it empty does not slow the request.

fields.label: Screenshot or document
fields.helpText: A screenshot of the error, or the approval email for an access request.

fields.label: Phone for IT to reach you
fields.helpText: Only if IT should call rather than write.

forms.confirmation: Your IT request was received. IT Support will review it and assign it to a technician. You will be notified in Provia when the request is assigned, when IT needs more information from you, and when it is resolved. You can follow it at any time under My cases, where you can add comments or files.

access.path: signed-in employees via the workflow start / form entry (assumption, decision D1)

forms.title: Resolution confirmation
forms.responsePolicy: single response; maps values and completes the action

decisions.question: Access model for the intake form: signed-in employees only, or an external link? Anonymous submission is not offered until the configured form behaviour is checked. If an external link is chosen, add requester_name and requester_email fields and revisit the organization grant.
Which team handles IT requests, its real name and members; does it need to see every IT case (a view grant as a shared queue) or only its assigned ones?
Department list (to turn `department` into a select) and the final `request_type` option list.
Response and resolution targets, if any, to state in the confirmation and to set as `due` on triage and resolve. None is promised until confirmed.
Confirmation screen capabilities in the destination form configuration: custom text, display of the case reference, redirect.
Route when the requester answers 'not solved' in the resolution confirmation: return to resolve, or an IT decision.
Country, language, timezone and currency of the organization. Angola, English response with pt-AO labels, Africa/Luanda and AOA are provisional.
